He confirmed that the main work of establishing the proposed medical college will begin within the next few months.
He made these remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inauguration ceremony of an eye camp with Nepal's assistance at Thakurgaon Diabetic and Healthcare Hospital on Sunday morning.
He said: "Since the majority of people in our region are poor, it is not possible for many to travel to Dhaka for treatment. The government is working sincerely to reach modern healthcare to the doorsteps of these ordinary and marginalized people."
He further said that the present government has organized such eye camps through bilateral discussions with the Nepalese government, which will play a role in providing better services to eye patients in the area.
He also said that a decision will be taken after discussing how to expand the scope of such eye camps in each upazila of the district in phases.
Mirza Fakhrul said: "To improve the quality of healthcare in the area, the 250-bed Thakurgaon General Hospital has already been upgraded to 600 beds. We are trying to improve the quality of healthcare and how to reach the facilities to the doorsteps of the common people."
The guest of honour of the event, Deputy Chief of Mission of the Embassy of Nepal to Bangladesh, Pratik Karki, in his speech said the relations between Nepal and Bangladesh are tied with a strong thread of historical bond.
“This relationship is not only between the government of Nepal and the government of Bangladesh but it extends to the people of Bangladesh and the people of Nepal. This relationship is of friendship and mutual cooperation in all fields including agriculture, industry, trade, healthcare, culture,” He said.
Padma Narayan Chowdhury, Chairman of Biratnagar Eye Hospital, Nepal, Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Rafiqul Haque, Superintendent of Police, Belal Hossain, District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin, among others were present.

item.title: Iran media denies Trump claim that Tehran asked US not to strike
item.description:
Iran’s Mehr news agency on Sunday denied President Donald Trump’s claim that the Islamic republic asked the United States to refrain from conducting new strikes.
Citing military officials, the agency said the allegation “was nothing but a new lie” and that the Iranian armed forces were “on high alert and ready for any eventuality.”
On Saturday, Trump said the US was “ready to go against the Islamic republic” but that Tehran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked him to hold off on fresh strikes.
He said he had made the decision, subject to reaching a deal with Iran.
“This would include the Immediate,Complete andTotal OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat,” wrote Trump in a Truth Social post.
On Sunday, Iran’s Fars news agency, citing a source close to Iranian negotiators said, “as long as the United States maintains its hostile actions, the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed.”
Iran has blockaded Hormuz since the start of the war, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.

item.title: DU undergraduate admission applications open November 11
item.description:
Online applications for undergraduate admission at the University of Dhaka for the 2026–2027 academic session will open at 12pm on November 11 and close at 11:59pm on November 25.
The decisions were finalized on Sunday, at a meeting of the General Admission Committee held at the Nabab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Bhaban auditorium. Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr ABM Obaidul Islam chaired the meeting.
Also present were Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academic) Professor Dr. Abdus Salam, Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Professor Dr. Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane, Treasurer Professor Dr. M. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, the convener of the Online Admission Committee, deans of various faculties, provosts of the residential halls, chairs of academic departments, directors of institutes, and other concerned officials.
Undergraduate admission tests for 2026–2027 will be held under five units: the Faculty of Arts, Law and Social Sciences Unit, the Science Unit, the Business Studies Unit, the Fine Arts Unit, and the IBA Unit.
The meeting also fixed the admission test schedule:
Science Unit — Saturday, December 12, 2026
IBA Unit — Saturday, December 5, 2026
Fine Arts Unit (general knowledge and drawing) — Tuesday, December 22, 2026
Arts, Law and Social Sciences Unit — Saturday, December 19, 2026
Business Studies Unit — Saturday, December 26, 2026
Except for the IBA Unit, all admission tests will run from 11:00 am to 12:30 pm. The IBA Unit test will be held from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon.
Tests for three units — Arts, Law and Social Sciences; Science; and Business Studies — will be held not only in Dhaka but also in eight divisional cities, at Rajshahi University, Chittagong University, Barisal University, Khulna University, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh Agricultural University in Mymensingh, and Begum Rokeya University. The Fine Arts and IBA units will be tested in Dhaka only.
For every unit except Fine Arts and IBA, the test will carry 60 marks for MCQs and 40 for the written portion. In the Fine Arts Unit, MCQs will be worth 40 marks and the drawing test 60 marks. The IBA Unit will carry 70 marks for MCQs and 30 for a descriptive test.
Fine Arts Unit — 30 minutes for MCQs, 60 minutes for drawing/written
IBA Unit — 90 minutes for MCQs, 30 minutes for the descriptive test
All other units — 45 minutes for MCQs, 45 minutes for the written portion
Candidates will be evaluated out of 120 marks in total — 100 from the admission test itself, and 20 based on SSC/equivalent and HSC/equivalent results.
Applicants must have passed their SSC or equivalent examination between 2021 and 2024, and their HSC or equivalent examination in 2026.
Science Unit: Combined GPA (including the 4th subject) in SSC and HSC or equivalent must be at least 8, with a minimum of 3.5 in each separately. Students from the Humanities and Business Studies streams under the HSC and Madrasah boards may also apply, provided their combined GPA is at least 7.5, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately.
Arts, Law and Social Sciences Unit: Combined GPA must be at least 7.5, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately. Students from the Science and Business Studies streams under the HSC and Madrasah boards may also apply — for Science-stream applicants, the combined GPA must be at least 8.0, with a minimum of 3.5 in each separately; for Business Studies-stream applicants, at least 7.5 combined, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately.
Business Studies Unit: Combined GPA must be at least 7.5, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately. Students from the Science and Humanities streams under the HSC and Madrasah boards may also apply — for Science-stream applicants, the combined GPA must be at least 8.0, with a minimum of 3.5 in each separately; for Humanities-stream applicants, at least 7.5 combined, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately.
Fine Arts Unit: Combined GPA must be at least 6.5, with a minimum of 3.0 in each separately.
The meeting also decided that, for the Science Unit, a separate question paper will be set for English-medium students, aligned with their curriculum.
Classes for the 2026–2027 undergraduate session are set to begin on March 28, 2027.

item.title: Centuries-old bamboo craft fights for survival in Dinajpur
item.description:
The centuries-old tradition of bamboo craft in the northern district Dinajpur is fast fading, as modern lifestyles, high prices and declining demand drive artisans away from their ancestral trade.
A visit to the traditional Setabganj market in Bochaganj upazila found artisans grappling with shrinking demand, soaring bamboo prices and limited market access, leaving many unable to recover even their production costs.
As earnings continue to decline, a growing number of craftsmen are abandoning their ancestral profession for day labour, farming and battery-powered three-wheeler driving.
"We once made a decent living from bamboo work. Now it is no longer enough to support a family, and our children have no interest in continuing the trade," said veteran artisan Biplab Pal, who has been engaged in the craft for nearly 40 years.
Long-time craftsmen Mahesh Chandra Roy and Anil Pal shared similar concerns, saying they continue the profession largely to preserve a family tradition despite earning only nominal profits.
Another artisan, Nikhil Sarkar, said financial hardship forced him to steer his eldest son into another occupation.
Yet amid the industry's decline, a handful of craftsmen are finding new opportunities through innovation.
Artisan Shafiqul Islam has introduced colourful finishes and contemporary designs to traditional bamboo products, helping attract younger buyers and improve sales.
"Customers now prefer modern-looking products. By redesigning traditional bamboo items, I've been able to increase both demand and profits," he said.
Young entrepreneur Arif Hossain said bamboo craftsmanship represents an important part of Bangladesh's cultural heritage and should be preserved through better planning, modern product development and stronger government support.
Artisans and local stakeholders recommend design and skills training, easy-access loans for small producers and expanded commercial bamboo cultivation to ensure a stable supply of raw materials.
Deputy General Manager of the Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) in Dinajpur, Md Jahedul Islam, said modernization is key to reviving the sector.
He said BSCIC provides three-month training programmes to enhance artisans' skills, along with loan facilities and regular monitoring to help make bamboo-based enterprises commercially sustainable.
Without effective policy support and sustained institutional backing, artisans fear Dinajpur's once-thriving bamboo craft industry could soon become little more than a fading memory.

item.title: At least 72 died in Spain’s Ceuta migrant rush
item.description:
At least 72 people died during the mass influx in recent days of migrants into Spain’s Ceuta enclave, when tens of thousands of people mostly swam around the border post from Morocco, local officials said on Sunday.
Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Spain’s north African territory have returned to Morocco since the territory’s largest mass migrant crossing.
“The latest figure that we have is 72,” the government’s delegate to Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez Triano, told reporters when asked about the number of fatalities.
The previous toll was 67 deaths.
Spanish police and troops patrolled the streets of Ceuta on Sunday as the enclave largely returned to normal after the sudden mass influx of migrants from Morocco that had occurred between Wednesday and Friday.
Only small groups of migrants were still walking around after most who crossed the small border barrier returned voluntarily to Morocco in 48 hours.
AFP on Saturday saw migrant minors milling around in a disused industrial park in Ceuta. Others were seen dozing on the pavements outside.
“All the children here want to go to (mainland) Spain,” said one of the few adults at the site, Moroccan man Aziz Dabch, 41.
The largest migrant rush into the enclave has caused an international crisis for Spain, with European partners criticizing Madrid for its immigration policies.
Outside a housing project near Ceuta port, Spanish soldiers detained a group of nine tired-looking migrants who were sitting on the pavement, guarded by troops with an armored car, an AFP reporter said.
Small inflatable boats from a rescue unit scoured the waters around the border barrier that extends into the Mediterranean Sea, where a new 500-meter floating boom reinforced security.
The Civil Guard was also taking migrants off a bus to escort them back to the border post to return to Morocco.
The border crossing was calm, with groups of workers picking up trash, clothes and rubbish left behind during the mass crossing.
Spain has blamed criminal gangs for spreading rumors that a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on immigration would allow migrants easier passage.
Some analysts suggested Morocco could allow migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain, which has recently improved ties with Rabat’s archenemy, neighboring Algeria.
In 2021, around 10,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta, taking advantage of Morocco easing border controls as a way to pressure Spain.
Moroccan officials have so far not offered any statement on the crisis.
But some of those who crossed the border said they had heard the border was open -- a rumor quickly amplified on social media.
The EU said it would hold a video call on Tuesday after 22 bloc members issued a joint open letter calling for an urgent meeting to agree on a speedy coordinated response and to prevent further uncontrolled crossings.
Italy on Saturday implemented a one-month suspension of its Schengen agreement with Spain, allowing for visa-free movement between borders.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, in a letter to EU leaders, blasted the “selfish” reaction by some EU countries.
Pope Leo XIV on Sunday spoke to the situation in Ceuta in his daily prayers on Sunday, saying he was following it “with concern” and hoping for a solution of “peace, stability, and justice”.

item.title: Thousands told to evacuate as wildfires worsen in Washington state
item.description:
A fast-moving wildfire neared the US city of Spokane on Saturday, forcing thousands of residents to evacuate as Washington state declared an emergency over one of its worst fire seasons on record.
More than 200,000 acres were burning across the northwestern state during a record fourth consecutive year of statewide drought. “Our record-setting drought and high winds are creating dangerous conditions across the state,” Governor Bob Ferguson said in a statement, adding that most outdoor and agricultural burning were banned through the end of September. “This year has already been one of our busiest wildfire years on record, and we just started August,” said Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove.
A wildfire dubbed the Old Trails fire jumped the Spokane River on Saturday afternoon and crossed into the city, the Spokesman-Review newspaper reported.
Authorities issued the highest-level evacuation alert, “Go Now," for swathes of northern Spokane affecting thousands of people within city limits, according to the government’s evacuation map.
The fire grew to more than 3,500 acres by 8:20pm, according to the Spokesman-Review. City officials did not report any injuries. “When the sun sets and the sun rises, we are going to be in shock,” Major General Gent Welsh told a news conference. Emergency authorities set up a fire evacuation shelter at the Spokane Convention Center.
Earlier in the day, the National Weather Service declared a “particularly dangerous situation” Red Flag Alert, which called the weather risk “extreme” across Eastern Washington.
The Washington National Guard said on X it was “rapidly mobilizing units” to assist Spokane.

item.title: Power returns to Cuba’s west after grid failure
item.description:
Power returned to Havana and other parts of western Cuba early Sunday after the latest in a string of widespread grid failures was fixed by the state-run electric company.
Five of 15 provinces spent most of the night without electricity due to a “partial collapse” of the electricity grid, but the power was being restored, Cuba’s UNE said on X.
Cuba is reeling from its worst economic crisis in decades—one made worse by a fuel blockade imposed by US President Donald Trump since January.
Trump has mounted a pressure campaign aimed at ending six decades of communist rule in Cuba.
UNE says the fuel shortages have made the national grid more susceptible to outages and rendered the use of emergency generators—which typically run on diesel fuel—all but impossible.
In recent weeks, blackouts have lasted more than 30 hours in Havana and for several days in other parts of the island, which is believed to have a population of over nine million people.
Since the start of 2026, Cuba has experienced five nationwide blackouts, three of them in July within a period of 10 days.
Since late 2024, there have been 10 such total power outages.
Cubans are not shy about admitting that they are weary of the constant disruptions to daily life.
“We live practically like fireflies here—in the dark all the time. You never know when you’ll have power. It’s our sad reality,” Julian Gonzalez, a 72-year-old carpenter, told AFP.
Like many Havana residents who live near the Malecon, a coastal esplanade and seawall in the capital, Gonzalez was out trying to catch a bit of fresh air.
“It’s better than sitting at home feeling bitter,” he said.
Havana blames Washington’s punitive measures for the dire state of its electricity grid, while the US says the fault lies with Cuba’s government and mismanagement of the economy.
The seven thermal power plants that form the national grid’s backbone have all been in operation for more than 40 years, and are in various states of disrepair.
Relations between Washington and Havana have been tensed since the start of the year, especially since US forces snatched Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro from Caracas in early January and took him to the US to face federal charges.
Maduro had long been a staunch ally of Cuba, providing cut-rate fuel.
Washington has authorized the arrival of only one Russian tanker—carrying 100,000 tons of crude—which came in March. Those reserves have since been exhausted.
In addition to its oil blockade, the Trump administration has ramped up sanctions against Cuban state-owned businesses, prompting many foreign businesses to suspend operations in the country.
The United States has also indicted former president Raul Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader Fidel Castro, over the downing of two civilian planes three decades ago.
In late June, Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said “no progress” had been made in months of bilateral discussions.
But under pressure from all of the US measures, Cuban lawmakers adopted a raft of free-market reforms aimed at rolling back the state’s role in the economy and attracting investment in everything from banking to tourism and agriculture.
And on Wednesday, Havana said it would open up major sectors such as gas stations, electricity generation, trash collection, and pharmacies to private firms.
